questions.q: What question does a metric answer that a log doesn't?
options: How something is behaving over time, in aggregate — like whether an error rate is trending up
Exactly which specific event got stuck in which stage
The exact detailed content of a single error at a specific moment
Metrics and logs answer exactly the same question
questions.explain: A metric can tell you that something's wrong, but not why — that's what logs are for.

questions.q: What does a trace provide that neither logs nor metrics do?
options: How one specific event moved through every stage of the pipeline
An aggregate view of behavior over time
The exact error message for a single moment
A summary of Fabric Capacity billing
questions.explain: Tracing every single event would be far too much data to store or read through, which is why it's used selectively.

questions.q: What does the Monitoring Hub (Lesson 16) provide, and what does it NOT provide?
options: It provides unified run history and basic metrics/logging built in, but not the detailed, per-event tracing across every pipeline stage
It provides full distributed tracing for every single event, out of the box
It only shows Power BI report usage statistics
It replaces the need for any KQL-based metrics or logs
questions.explain: Following one specific trip event through every stage needs purpose-built tracing beyond what the Monitoring Hub gives by default.

questions.q: In a real incident, what's the typical order for checking observability pillars?
options: Start with a metric or alert noticing something's off, move to logs for the specific error, and reach for a trace only when the failure spans multiple stages
Always start with a full distributed trace before checking anything else
Always start with raw logs, regardless of what triggered the investigation
There's no reasonable order — all three should always be checked simultaneously
questions.explain: Starting with the wrong pillar wastes time — like building a trace for a problem a single log line already explains.

questions.q: Why doesn't a metric replace the need for logs?
options: A metric shows aggregate trends but can't show the exact detail of what happened at a specific moment
Metrics and logs are actually the exact same thing with different names
Logs are always less useful than metrics in every situation
Metrics only work with batch pipelines, never streaming ones
questions.explain: Neither pillar replaces the others — each answers a genuinely different question about the system's behavior.
